answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments bind identity to singular non-transferable proofs, preventing malicious actors from allowing their illicit influence to wander across fragmented sub-graphs. By mandating a verifiable delay function as a relic of proof-of-work history, the system enforces sequential computational bottlenecks that preclude rapid identity cloning. Adversaries face negative expected utility, as staking collateral subjected to slashing penalties makes the fable of mass Sybil exploitation a prohibitively expensive cryptoeconomic impossibility.
